**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/28 (Sun) 07:14  
[FACT] User is seeking information on setting the Windows hostname on an EC2 instance.  
[FACT] User's EC2 instance is joined to AWS Managed Active Directory.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To set the Windows hostname on an EC2 instance at startup when it is joined to AWS Managed Active Directory, leverage user data scripts and PowerShell.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 1: Launch a new Windows EC2 instance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 2: In the 'Configure Instance Details' step, expand the 'Advanced Details' section at the bottom.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Step 3: In the 'User data' field, enter a PowerShell script to set the hostname and join the instance to the domain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User data script placeholder values include: YOUR_HOSTNAME, YOUR_DOMAIN_NAME, DOMAIN_USER, and DOMAIN_PASSWORD.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] PowerShell script provided by the assistant:  
```powershell
<powershell>
$hostname = "YOUR_HOSTNAME"
$domainName = "YOUR_DOMAIN_NAME"
$domainUser = "DOMAIN_USER"
$domainPassword = "DOMAIN_PASSWORD"

# Set the hostname
Rename-Computer -NewName $hostname -Force
Restart-Computer -Force

# Wait for the instance to restart
Start-Sleep -s 60

# Join the instance to the domain
$securePassword = ConvertTo-SecureString -String $domainPassword -AsPlainText -Force
$domainCreds = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential ($domainName + "\" + $domainUser, $securePassword)
Add-Computer -DomainName $domainName -Credential $domainCreds -Restart -Force
</powershell>
```  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The provided user data script will set the hostname of the instance, restart the instance to apply the new hostname, and join the instance to the specified domain using the provided domain user and password.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The script assumes the EC2 instance has access to the AWS Managed Active Directory.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User may need to configure security groups and network settings to ensure proper connectivity.
